For people who design and deliver programs

Make the whole process easier to complete.

Four places to investigate in your own program. Each connects a barrier to an action and a measure.

01

Find out

People can qualify without knowing a program exists.

Make it easier

Explain who the program is for in plain language. Give partners a direct referral with a clear next step.

Measure it

Of people referred, how many reach the service and finish enrollment?

02

Apply

Unclear requirements turn one application into repeated calls and visits.

Make it easier

Show accepted information before someone starts. Offer accessible formats, language support and help. Reuse verified information where permitted.

Measure it

Time to a decision, repeated document requests, and where people stop.

03

Use the benefit

Approval alone does not make a benefit practical to use.

Make it easier

Check service locations, opening hours, transportation and digital access. Explain restrictions where people encounter them.

Measure it

Failed attempts, distance to service, and issued benefits actually used.

04

Keep receiving it

Recurring requirements can interrupt support for people who still qualify.

Make it easier

Send understandable reminders. Identify what needs updating, reuse current information where allowed, and offer flexible contact options.

Measure it

Renewal among still-eligible people, interruptions, and reasons for leaving.

WIC: one example behind these practices

WIC illustrates how enrollment steps, retailer access and recurring requirements can affect practical access. These findings should not be assumed to apply identically to another program.

Read the evidence and its limitations

These are actions to evaluate, not a validated score or promises of a particular effect. Avoid collecting personal data you don’t need.
